newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina opens bank files for Nazi gold hunt.
newsitem.headline: Argentina opens bank files for Nazi gold hunt.

text.p: President Carlos Menem invited Argentina's Jewish community on Tuesday to search Central Bank archives for evidence that Jewish gold stolen by the Nazis had found its way to Argentina.

Ruben Beraja, leader of one of the world's largest Jewish communities, said after meeting the Peronist president that Menem "asked us to speed up the probe and told us Central Bank archives are open for investigation by anyone interested."

Beraja, vice president of the World Jewish Congress, told reporters that Argentina "was one of the transit routes and probably a tranfer point" for Nazi gold, according to what he described as U.S. intelligence data.

Interest in the fate of the huge wealth plundered from Holocaust victims has been heightened by a British Foreign Office report alleging that the Swiss kept most of the gold the Nazis put in secret bank accounts during the Second World War.
The Simon Wiesenthal Centre, a Jewish organisation in Los Angeles that hunts down Nazi war criminals, has urged Argentina to open its Central Bank files for investigation.
Argentina was a safe haven for such notorious Nazi war criminals as Holocaust architect Adolf Eichmann and SS Captain Erich Priebke, who was extradited to Italy.

More recently it has been criticised for failing to find the perpetrators of two major anti-Jewish bomb attacks -- one at the Israeli Embassy in 1992 that killed 29 people and another at a Jewish community centre in 1994 that killed 86 people.
